# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is a **qualitative analysis of the free-text and multi-select answers**
of the International RSE Survey 2026. Many survey questions let respondents type
their own answers ("other, please specify") or pick several options. 
This book turns those raw responses into a small set of meaningful categories 
and presents them as summary tables (and, for multi-select questions, heatmaps).

Each chapter covers **one survey question**. The analysis can be focused on a
single country or a set of countries through one configuration value
(`FILTER`) in `R\.config`, so the same code can produce, for example, a Nordic 
view or a German view of every question.

# The general idea

For every question the workflow is the same:

1. **Load and filter** the raw survey data for the configured country/countries.
2. **Tokenize** the responses (split comma-separated answers, lowercase, trim).
3. **Recode** the raw responses into categories using a per-chapter
   regular-expression map (`recode_map`).
4. **Summarize** the categories into a frequency/percentage table.
5. **Audit** the recoding with a raw-to-category allocation table, which is
   collected in the @sec-appendix-recoding appendix so every categorization
   decision is transparent and reproducible.

# Folder and file overview

The book lives in `rse-book/` and is organized as follows:

+ `index.qmd`: This page (preface and usage guide).
+ `_quarto.yml`: Book configuration (chapter order, output format, execution
  options).
+ `chapters/`: One `.qmd` file per survey question (the analysis chapters).
+ `appendices/`:
    + `methodology.qmd`: Data and methodology notes.
    + `recoding.qmd`: The codebook, i.e. the raw-to-category allocation tables
      collected from all chapters.
+ `R/`: The shared R code.
    + `.config`: User configuration (data directory and country filter).
    + `postprocessing.R`: All analysis and plotting functions
      (`process_text_codes_with_allocation()`, `plot_heatmap()`, the data
      loading helpers, table renderers, etc.).
    + `_common.R` / `_load_common.R`: Setup sourced by every chapter; it loads
      the configuration, the analysis functions, and the question metadata.
+ `references.bib` / `references.qmd`: Bibliography (currently empty).
+ `_book/`: Rendered output (generated, not edited by hand).
+ `_freeze/` and `_allocation_cache/`: Generated caches (see
  [Caching and rebuilds]).

The **raw survey data** is *not* inside `rse-book/`. It lives in a separate
directory at the repository root (default `RSE_survey_2026_data/`). The
analysis reads just two files there: `2026_tf.csv` (the full respondent table,
one row per respondent, used for both country filtering via `socio1_0` and for
selecting each question's columns) and `2026_all_cols.csv` (question metadata,
used to decode multi-response option labels).

# Setup the config file

All user configuration is in `rse-book/R/.config`. It is plain R that is
`source()`d at the start of every chapter:

+ `DATA_DIR`: the directory name where the raw survey data lives
  (default `RSE_survey_2026_data`).
+ `FILTER`: which respondents to include. This can be:
    + a **single country**, e.g. `FILTER = "Germany"`, or
    + a **set of countries**, e.g. the Nordics:
      `FILTER = c("Finland", "Norway", "Sweden", "Denmark", "Iceland", "Estonia")`.

Whatever you set here becomes the default country scope for every chapter.

::: {.callout-tip}
You can also analyze a different country for a single table or plot without
touching the config, by passing `filter =` directly to the functions, e.g.
`plot_heatmap("Germany", "currentEmp13")` or
`process_text_codes_with_allocation(filter = c("Sweden", "Norway"), ...)`.
This is handy for comparing countries side by side in one chapter. As is done
for example in the chapters `currentEmp13` and `conf2can_0`.
:::

# Anatomy of a chapter

Each chapter in `chapters/` follows the same pattern:

1. **Front matter** with the question title and `question_id`.
2. A setup cell that loads the shared code:

```{{r}}
#| include: false
#| file: ../R/_load_common.R
```

3. (Multi-select questions) a **heatmap** of who selected what:

```{{r}}
#| echo: false
plot_heatmap(FILTER, "tool4can")
```

4. A **recode map**: a `tibble` of `raw` (regex) and `clean` (category) pairs.
   A row with `NA` in `clean` excludes matching responses from the analysis.

5. The **analysis call**, which produces the summary table and caches the
   allocation (audit) table for the recoding appendix:

```{{r}}
#| echo: false
data_coded <- process_text_codes_with_allocation(
  filter = FILTER,
  question_code = "tool4can",
  recode_map = recode_map,
  header = "Software Languages",
  other = TRUE,
  cache_id = "tool4"
)

data_coded$summary_table
```

Useful arguments:

+ `question_code`: the question code, i.e. the column-name stem in
  `2026_tf.csv` (e.g. `"conf2can_0"`, or `"org2can"` for the `org2can[...]_0`
  multi-response sub-columns). The helpers select the matching columns and
  decode option labels automatically.
+ `other`: `TRUE` for the "other, please specify" free-text responses, `FALSE`
  for the main pre-defined options.
+ `cache_id`: an identifier under which the allocation table is saved so it
  appears in the @sec-appendix-recoding appendix.

All code cells use `#| echo: false`, so the rendered book shows tables and
figures but not the underlying R code.

# How to run

You need [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and R (with the
packages used in `R/postprocessing.R`: `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `stringr`, `purrr`,
`forcats`, `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `gt`, `scales`, `tibble`).

Run the commands from inside the `rse-book/` directory:

```bash
cd rse-book
```

## Run a single chapter

```bash
quarto render chapters/conf2can_0.qmd
```

The result is written to `_book/chapters/conf2can_0.html`.

## Run the entire book

```bash
quarto render
```

Then open `_book/index.html`.

## Update the recoding appendix

The codebook in `appendices/recoding.qmd` is built from allocation tables that
the **chapters** produce while they render. So render the chapters first (e.g.
render the whole book), then refresh the appendix:

```bash
quarto render appendices/recoding.qmd --no-cache
```

# Caching and rebuilds

+ **`_freeze/`** (`freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml`): Quarto re-executes a chapter
  only when its source changes. If you change the data or the shared R code and
  a chapter looks stale, re-render it (or delete its `_freeze/` entry) to force
  re-execution.
+ **`_allocation_cache/`**: each chapter writes its allocation table here (keyed
  by `cache_id`); the recoding appendix reads them back. If you rename or remove
  questions, you may want to clear stale `.rds` files here.
